newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan welcomes Iraq oil-for-food deal.
newsitem.headline: Japan welcomes Iraq oil-for-food deal.

text.p: Japan on Tuesday welcomed the start of a long-delayed oil-for-food deal between the United Nations and Iraq, but cautioned that the accord did not signify Baghdad's immediate return to the global community.

"Japan supports the U.N. 986 resolution from a humanitarian point of view, and hopes the resolution accomplishes its purpose of alleviating the suffering of the Iraqi people," Foreign Ministry spokesman Hiroshi Hashimoto said in a statement.

"However, for Iraq to be accepted into the international community once more, and for peace and stability to return to the Gulf area...we strongly demand that Iraq continue to observe its obligations under related Security Council resolutions," the statement said.

The United Nations on Monday authorised the start of the oil-for-food deal with Iraq, enabling Baghdad to make a limited return to the world oil market for the first time since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Security Council resolution 986, passed in April 1995, allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other necessities for its people, who have been suffering from sanctions imposed in August 1990.
The plan was concluded in May but has been held up by disputes over implementation.
The initial six-month period began on Tuesday.
